findings.issue: vue-router is declared as a direct dependency solely for the LocationQueryRaw type (app/app/pages/index.vue:2) while Nuxt already provides it transitively; the pin also rides the newest patch (5.4.0, 2026-10-07), which recently shipped an experimental-surface breaking change (query values normalized to arrays).
findings.suggestion: Drop the direct vue-router dependency and import the type from Nuxt's re-exports (e.g. '#vue-router'/'#app' type surface) or define the small query object type locally, letting Nuxt manage the router version.

findings.issue: nuxt ^4.6.2 was released 2026-10-16, two weeks before review, and is tracking the tip of the stable line rather than an established minor.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable since it is a stable release, but for a long-lived codebase consider whether pinning to the very latest patch immediately (vs waiting for a few patch iterations) is the desired policy; either way, no experimental APIs are enabled.

summary: The app uses exclusively long-stable Nuxt 4, Nitro, Vue and vue-router APIs — no experimental flags, unstable_ names, or preview features appear anywhere, verified against the framework's current stable releases (Nuxt 4.6.x, vue-router 5.4.x). It even avoids vue-router 5's newly experimental surface (definePage, data loaders, typed query params) while depending on v5. Risk of breaking-change churn from experimental APIs is essentially zero.
